title: Client Communication Trigger
description: Tells the client communication specialist what to draft and why. The scenario_type drives which template and tone to use. GAP 3 FIX: Explicit scenario types from the client brief prevent generic drafts that don't match the situation.

trigger_type.description: High-level category. Determines which section of rules.md applies.

scenario_type.description: GAP 3 FIX: Each value maps to a specific template and tone. missed_showing = apologetic + immediate reschedule. competing_offer = calm urgency + agent recommends position. inspection_issue = factual + options-forward. financing_delay = reassuring + clear next steps. Never use 'general' — if you can't identify the scenario, escalate.

assigned_agent.description: The specialist drafts in THIS agent's voice — not Diana's, not a generic agent.

preferred_contact.description: Drives format: email = formal, text = conversational, phone = talking points only.

relationship_stage.description: Affects warmth and assumed familiarity in the draft.

scenario_details.description: Plain-English description of what happened. E.g. 'Inspection found HVAC needs replacement, estimated $8,000.'

recommended_position.description: What the transaction coordinator recommends the agent communicate as the negotiation position. Client_communication includes this in the draft.

deadline.description: If there is a response deadline, include it. The draft should reference it explicitly.

research_brief_ref.description: handoff_id of the research_brief if relevant to this communication.
